question: The pressure exerted on a body is 10 Nm⁻², if the area of the body is 2 m² : then the thrust acting on the body will be:
solution:
The Correct answer is __**20 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the force exerted per unit area of a surface.
 
• The formula for calculating pressure is **Pressure = Force/Area**.
 
• In this case, the pressure is given as **10 N/m²** and the area of the body is **2 m²**.
 
• To find the thrust (or force) acting on the body, we use the formula **Thrust = Pressure × Area**.
 
• Substituting the values into the formula: **Thrust = 10 × 2 = 20 N**.
 
• The thrust acting on the body is therefore **20 N**, which corresponds to the correct option.
 
• Thrust is a term used to describe the total force exerted perpendicular to a surface.
 
• This concept is important in mechanics and fluid dynamics to understand the interaction between forces and surfaces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pressure**__

 __
 
• **Pressure** is measured in units of **Newton per square meter (N/m²)**, also known as **Pascals (Pa)**.
 
• It is widely used in areas such as **engineering, physics, fluid mechanics, and material science**.
 
• Pressure is a scalar quantity, meaning it has magnitude but no direction.
 
 
 
• **Thrust**__
 __
 
• **Thrust** is a term used to describe the perpendicular force exerted by a body on a surface.
 
• It is commonly discussed in the context of **aerodynamics, fluid dynamics, and propulsion systems**.
 
• Thrust is measured in units of **Newton (N)**, which is the standard unit for force in the International System of Units (SI).
 
 
 
• **Area**__
 
 
• **Area** is a measure of the surface covered by a shape or object.
 
• It is expressed in square units such as **m²** in the SI system.
 
• Understanding area is essential for calculations involving **pressure, thrust, and energy distribution**.
